_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. First print press 4.33.5 (run 20261014-153356-31994c0c); first release on press 4.34.2 (run 20261027-171145-29bd3631). Credential-less: no vendor PBX; behaviour proven against a mock PBX built from 3CX's official XAPI swagger.

handfixes.summary: Root help reads '3CX CLI', not the slug-derived 'Threecx CLI'
handfixes.why: root.go.tmpl renders {{humanName .Name}} and ignores the spec's x-display-name (press 4.33.5 and 4.34.2). Re-apply: cli-factory/threecx/reprint-4342-20261027/tools/apply_handfixes.py.

handfixes.summary: The unresolved {fqdn} error also tells the user to pick a registered PBX with --pbx
handfixes.why: The generated TemplateVarError only says 'export THREECX_FQDN=<value>'; fleet users and agents never learn about --pbx from the error they actually hit.

asserts.contains: or pick a registered phone system with --pbx <name>

handfixes.summary: Every API request, redirect hop and the OAuth token exchange go only to the scheme, host and port the configuration resolved when the client was built (for --pbx, the registered PBX's FQDN); anything else is refused before it is dialled or given the secret or token
handfixes.why: Work order host pinning. The generated client sends the bearer token to whatever URL a request names, and the token client (cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient) reuses the client's transport. originPinTripper (hand file internal/cli/threecx_guard.go, registered with registerClientHook so every CLI, fleet-child and MCP client gets it) compares a byte-exact ASCII-folded origin, and the same check runs first in CheckRedirect. Tests: TestOriginPinRefusesAnotherHost, TestNormalizedOriginRefusesNonASCIIAndFillsPorts, internal/threecxblackbox TestRedirectToAnotherHostIsRefused. Codex r1: the check is shared as pinnedRedirect, and the inner transport is sendOrRefuse (responses held, or every request refused under --dry-run). A redirect hop to a GET that mints, grants or allocates is refused unless the first request was one, since every confirm gate reads only the first path. Test: internal/threecxblackbox TestR4MCPRefusesARedirectToAStateChangingGET.

asserts.contains: c.HTTPClient.Transport = originPinTripper{origin: origin, next: sendOrRefuse(next, c.DryRun)}

handfixes.summary: The on-disk GET response cache is off on every client
handfixes.why: XAPI bodies carry SIP passwords, provisioning links and API keys; raw bodies must not sit in cache files (the store strips them separately). Set in guardClient. Test: internal/threecxblackbox TestNoCredentialInAnyWrittenFile.

handfixes.summary: Every store write passes withoutStoredSecrets at the merge choke point: credential-named values, PINs among them, are replaced by name at any depth, and a record that cannot be decoded is stored as {}. A held value anywhere else in a statement is refused by the kit (credkit-sqlite-every-handle).
handfixes.why: Every live read writes through to the store and sync upserts raw bodies. mergeIncomingResourceData is the one merge every upsert path calls. A PIN is never held, so nothing else would stop it. Hand file internal/store/threecx_secrets.go. Tests: internal/store TestStoreRedactsCredentialMembersByName; internal/threecxblackbox TestNoCredentialInAnyWrittenFile.

handfixes.summary: Every credential a response carries is held before any command reads the body, then replaced by name so the listing stays readable: the access token /connect/token mints, Concealed values, credential-named fields, and the value a minting function (GenerateApiKey, APIToken, GenerateAppToken, GenerateProvLink, GetMicrosoftAccessToken, GetOAuth) returns. A token exchange is left whole for the client; its token is held all the same. A password that is literally a word such as hidden is held: a mask is judged by shape only.
handfixes.why: The kit withholds a whole unit that repeats a held value, so a listing that carries a SIP password would print nothing if the member were not replaced first. The kit holds declared names; the shared walker also holds what no declared name can see (Concealed objects under any name, minted unnamed values). responseHoldTripper (threecx_guard.go) reads each response under the client size cap and decodes it as the client will (client/threecx_decode.go: Content-Encoding, BOM, XSSI). holdToolArguments is the same walker over MCP arguments. Tests: TestResponseCredentialsHeld, TestAWordIsNeverAMask; black-box TestShortPasswordSplitOrEncoded, TestShortPasswordAloneKeepsTheRecord, TestMCPPreviewHoldsANestedCredential. A PIN the operator supplies is held (HoldOperatorValues, operatorFieldNames, the PIN flags); a PIN in a response is replaced by name and named in Identifiers. Every member of a duplicate key and every document in a body is held (decodeDocuments).

handfixes.summary: Mirrored MCP tools that can change 3CX state (import, any later non-read-only command) preview with --dry-run and send only with confirm: true
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 gates threecx_execute on confirm natively, but the Cobra-tree mirror registers import with no confirm. RequireConfirmForMirroredWrites (hand file internal/mcp/cobratree/threecx_confirm.go), called right after RegisterAll, wraps every mirrored tool that is not read-only, not mcp:local-write and not export/sync/workflow archive/learnings forget/reject, so a command added later is gated by default. Only boolean true sends. Tests: TestRegisteredMirroredWritesNeedConfirm (fails without the tools.go line), internal/threecxblackbox TestMCPWriteNeedsConfirm (threecx_execute previews send nothing, confirm true sends one).

asserts.contains: if confirmed, ok := args["confirm"].(bool); ok && confirmed {

handfixes.summary: The token-endpoint client 'auth login' builds (root.go oauthHTTPClient) is pinned to the configured phone system's origin like every API client, holds what the token endpoint answers, and refuses every request under --dry-run; 'auth login', 'auth set-token' and 'auth logout' honour --dry-run (preview, nothing sent, read, saved or deleted)
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] credential-sent-to-another-host: auth login used client.NewPlainHTTPClient, which registerClientHook never reaches, and the generated same-origin redirect check compares against the token URL itself, so THREECX_TOKEN_URL=https://<other>/connect/token sent the client secret (HTTP Basic) to another host. Codex r1 [P1] preview-sends-anyway: auth login ignored --dry-run and saved the minted token. Edit in generated root.go re-applied by tools/apply_handfixes.py; guardTokenClient, dryRunTripper and the auth wrapper live in hand files internal/cli/threecx_guard.go and internal/cli/threecx_auth_dryrun.go. Tests: internal/threecxblackbox TestAuthLoginNeverLeavesTheConfiguredPBX, TestDryRunSendsNothing; internal/cli TestDryRunClientsRefuseEveryRequest.

asserts.contains: hc.Transport = originPinTripper{origin: origin, next: sendOrRefuse(next, dryRun)}

handfixes.summary: One rule for every fleet verdict (health checks, licence renewal window, version drift, backup flags): healthy only when every input it uses was reported; a missing input makes the verdict unknown (or keeps a worse one), never pass, warn or current, and never drops a row from a filtered report
handfixes.why: Codex r1 and r2 [P1] unknown-telemetry-reported-as-healthy (every 3CX field is nullable in vendor-docs/3cx-swagger.yaml): a null IsMaintananceExpired read as current, a far licence date hid a null maintenance expiry in 'fleet licences --within', a null LicenseActive with a date passed. Orchestrator order 2026-10-27: fix the class structurally, test first. fleet.Settle (hand file internal/fleet/threecx_inputs.go) is the one rule; EvaluateHealth applies it to every check (licence activation and expiry, maintenance, backup schedule, trunks, flags, disk, storage quota, capacity incl. a limit of 0), LicenceRow.OutsideWindow drops a row only when activation and both expiries were reported (Unknown names the rest), VersionRowFor calls maintenance current only when both sources say so and a missing update list unknown, BackupRowFor flags SIZE_UNKNOWN when the shrink comparison lacks a size. Tests (seen failing first: unknown-seen-failing-unit.log, unknown-seen-failing-cli.log): TestHealthIsPassOnlyWhenEveryInputWasReported (every input nulled and dropped), TestLicenceOutsideWindowNeedsEveryInput, TestVersionVerdictsNeedEveryInput, TestFleetLicencesWithinKeepsPartialFacts, TestFleetVersionsBehindKeepsPartialFacts; prove_unknown.sh reverts each part alone.

asserts.contains: func Settle(level Level, detail string, missing ...string) (Level, string) {
settled("license", level, detail, unreported("licence activation", s.LicenseActive != nil, "licence expiry", ok))

handfixes.summary: The fleet runner re-executes only this binary (fleet.SelfExecutable = os.Executable; no caller can name another binary), with no shell, an argument list of fixed literals plus request paths re-validated as plain XAPI paths (childArgs), and a registry-validated PBX passed by name in the environment
handfixes.why: Security gate P1 at internal/fleet/runner.go (gosec G204, builtin exec-nonliteral-cmd). Orchestrator order 2026-10-27: remove it structurally if possible. The Runner.Exe override is gone (tests swap SelfExecutable); argv is built only by childArgs. gosec still reports G204 (the command is a variable by nature: the running binary's path), so the base-owned bound suppression in LEDGER-NOTES section 7 remains. Test: TestChildArgsAreFixedLiteralsAndValidatedPaths.

handfixes.summary: export --dry-run --output leaves the destination file untouched
handfixes.why: The generated export opened and truncated --output before the dry-run transport refused the first request, so a preview destroyed an existing export.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes GET /SystemStatus with the real credential (a client ID and secret it mints from count), refuses the shipped https://{fqdn}/xapi/v1 placeholder naming THREECX_FQDN and THREECX_BASE_URL, and reads a 404 as a wrong base URL, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one: it called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable", never probed the credential ("present, not verified"), so a 401 on every call and a base_url aimed at the 3CX web client (every API path 404s) both read healthy. threecx is a new connector and never received the fleet's port (replay_handfixes.py only replays entries already in a connector's own ledger), so it is ported by hand to the press 4.34.2 shape and adapted: (1) a 3CX install authenticates with THREECX_CLIENT_ID / THREECX_CLIENT_SECRET and holds no bearer until the first request mints one, so cfg.AuthHeader() alone read every real install as 'auth: not configured' and skipped the probe; doctorCredentialAvailable counts the client ID and secret, for the auth row, the Step 2 guard and doctorProbeCredentials, and a refused credential keeps its 'refused' verdict. (2) The probe prefers GET /SystemStatus, the read the connector's own fleet health/versions/backups/licences already depend on; the generic walk would pick `aisettings get` (GET /AISettings), a feature endpoint where a 404 proves nothing about the base URL. (3) The placeholder remedy names THREECX_FQDN and THREECX_BASE_URL, and the placeholder credentials row no longer shares text with the api row: the output chokepoint holds the value of every credential-named member, with needles that value whole and its text after the first space, so the old 'skipped (base_url is a placeholder)' made '(base_url is a placeholder)' a held value and the api row that repeated it printed as '[text withheld ...]', hiding the remedy. The credentials row stays WARN-prefixed so --fail-on keeps its placeholder semantics (the api row still carries the error phrase). The chokepoint's name-based redaction still prints `credentials` as '[redacted]' in every state, so check_doctor_truth.py reads the redaction rather than the verdict there; the verdict's polarity in all four states (plus no-credential and a rejected client secret) is proven before the chokepoint by doctor_verdict_test.go. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: if cmdPath = doctorLeafForPath(root, nil, doctorPreferredProbePath); cmdPath != "" {
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorFQDNEnv + " to your phone system's FQDN, or " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to its full API root"
report["credentials"] = "WARN not checked: no phone system is chosen yet, so nothing was sent"
report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own funnel, chokepoint and SQLite wrapper. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; the API client and token client go through credkit.Transport under the origin pin; every file write except the 0600 credential store and config file goes through the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile is that declared exemption); stdout and stderr are the kit's pipes.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. A PBX FQDN is the operator's, so no hosted domain can be named: credentialFiles shows the kit this process's phone system (--pbx, THREECX_PBX, THREECX_FQDN, config) through THREECX_BASE_URL for the duration of Start, and AfterStart puts the variable back. When nothing resolves the kit allows no origin. The fleet registry is deliberately not a credential file: the kit holds every value in a file it is given, and the registry holds host names. Tests: internal/threecxblackbox (built binaries against a stub that echoes every credential in every encoding), writers_test TestEveryFileWriteGoesThroughTheKit, internal/credwire TestCredentialFilesHoldsWhatDeclarationsCannotName, TestAfterStartRestoresTheBaseURL, internal/cli TestDeclaredCredentialFlagsMatchTheCommands. A saved profile is held where loadProfileStore reads it (cliutil.HoldProfileStore), whichever home it came from; startup still holds the homes it can name. Test: internal/threecxblackbox TestR4ProfileHeldWhereItIsRead.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the credkit wiring from a per-connector declarations file, and let a declaration name an operator-chosen host as its origin, so a reprint keeps it by construction.

asserts.contains: if err := credkit.WriteFile(tmp, body, 0o600); err != nil {

handfixes.summary: Every SQLite handle goes through credkit.SQLDriver: internal/credsql registers the one driver and every sql.Open in store.go and platform/migration.go names it, the read-only opener included. The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to a DSN parameter credsql applies as each connection opens.
handfixes.why: A statement's text and bound values are a sink of their own, reads included. Replaces the connector-only withheldSQLiteDriver.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate store, migration and MCP sql opens against one kit-wrapped driver name, and express the MCP sql value cap as a connection-open setting.

asserts.contains: func OpenReadOnlyValueCapped(dbPath string, maxValueBytes int) (*Store, error) {

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing, then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it: a token holding the word unauthorized made a GET /mcp without Authorization return a piece of the held token.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the inner, kit-wrapped handler and only a write-free preflight runs before credkit.MCPHTTP.

handfixes.summary: A GET that mints or grants a credential or allocates an object needs confirm on MCP
handfixes.why: 3CX exposes GenerateApiKey, GetRequestHelpLink (grants vendor remote access), InitTrunk and others as GETs, which the generated table reads as reads, so threecx_read ran them with no confirm and under the read-only switch. internal/mcp/threecx_mint_gate.go marks them at init; code_orch.go stays template output. export.go refuses a function call in place of a record, so the mirrored export tool, which runs with no confirm, cannot reach one.

handfixes.summary: The MCP server applies THREECX_PBX, so its native tools use the phone system the kit was shown
handfixes.why: The CLI selector runs from root's pre-run, which the MCP server never runs: Declarations named the selected phone system while native tools loaded the global config and store. Re-apply in cmd/threecx-mcp/main.go run(). The selection keeps the server's own controls: the read-only and no-local-data switches (fleet.keptEnv) and the listener's bearer, allowed origins and companion path (ApplyMCPPBXSelection, hand file).

handfixes.summary: A credential on disk goes only to the phone system it was saved for
handfixes.why: The store recorded the unresolved template https://{fqdn}/xapi/v1 and compared origins only under --config, so THREECX_FQDN naming another client sent this client's secret there. config.go records the resolved URL and judges every load; internal/config/threecx_origin.go holds the rule. keepProfileCredential judges the store beside an explicit config by the same rule, and refuseFileCredentialsElsewhere drops [headers] with the scalars.

handfixes.summary: config.toml keeps only the FQDN of template_vars, and no path context can set the FQDN
handfixes.why: The sync path-context argument was merged into TemplateVars and the token save wrote it to config.toml, where the next start held it and refused to start.

handfixes.summary: A --stdin body is held before a generated command parses it
handfixes.why: 236 generated commands parse --stdin into a map, losing every member of a duplicate key but the last. The selector's pre-run in threecx_pbx_select.go calls holdStdinBody. The kit also holds the whole body and every line from StdinFlags in internal/credwire/declarations.go, which covers a body that does not parse.

handfixes.summary: The fleet tests' per-PBX child is the Go test binary itself (TestMain runs fakeChildMain when FAKE_3CX_FLEET_CHILD=1), not a bash script, so the fleet tests run on Windows.
handfixes.why: A #!/bin/bash child cannot be executed on Windows: every fleet test there failed with 'none of the N PBX(es) in scope could be read' (CI on PR #557). The marker has no THREECX_ prefix so fleet.Scrub passes it to the child. internal/cli/root_test.go is generated; its TestMain gains the two-line dispatch.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

asserts.contains: func (t *syncThroughput) rowsPerSec(now time.Time, rows int64) float64 {

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).
